I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same fields. That is what I trust most for my place, my age, and my labor. I want grain that I know how to manage, that sells easily, and that does not force me into complicated field work. Winter wheat fits my land and my habits, and summer maize follows it well after harvest. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care more about stable yield than saving seed. I will fertilize in a simple way, irrigate only when the crop really needs it, and keep pesticide sprays limited to the main disease and insect periods. For wheat, I will give more attention to base fertilizer, one or two waterings around jointing and grain filling, and weed and disease control. After wheat harvest, I will seed maize quickly, keep the soil disturbance low, feed it mainly with nitrogen plus some phosphorus and potassium, water it a couple of times if rain is short, and spray only when pest pressure is clear. I will keep the whole year simple, familiar, and steady because that is how I protect both yield and my own labor.
